examTitle: AZ-104: Microsoft Azure Administrator Practice Exam 1
description: 40-question scenario-based practice exam covering the five AZ-104 skill areas per Microsoft's official skills outline effective April 17, 2026: Manage Azure identities and governance (20-25%), Implement and manage storage (15-20%), Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20-25%), Implement and manage virtual networking (15-20%), Monitor and maintain Azure resources (10-15%).
author: Chris Buchanan

questions.question: An administrator needs to let a partner organization's employees sign in to a shared Microsoft Entra tenant using their own corporate credentials, without creating separate accounts for them. Which feature should the administrator use?
questions.explanation: B2B collaboration invites external users as guests who authenticate with their home organization's credentials, avoiding duplicate account creation.

questions.question: A company wants users to be automatically added to a Microsoft Entra group based on their department attribute, without an administrator manually adding them. What should be configured?

options.text: A dynamic membership group with a rule based on the department attribute
An assigned group with a scheduled PowerShell script

questions.explanation: Dynamic membership groups evaluate rules against user or device attributes and automatically add or remove members as those attributes change.

questions.question: Users are frequently locking themselves out because they forget their passwords, generating a high volume of help desk tickets. Which feature reduces this load while letting users regain access on their own?
questions.explanation: SSPR lets users verify their identity and reset their own password without contacting the help desk.

questions.question: A developer must be able to start, stop, and restart virtual machines in a specific resource group but must not be able to delete them or modify networking. Which approach satisfies this with the least administrative effort?

options.text: Assign the built-in Virtual Machine Contributor role at the subscription scope
Assign the built-in Virtual Machine Contributor role scoped to the resource group
Assign the Owner role scoped to the resource group
Add the developer to the Global Administrator role

questions.explanation: Scoping the built-in Virtual Machine Contributor role to the resource group grants VM start/stop/restart rights there only, without subscription-wide access.

questions.question: An administrator assigns a user the Reader role at the subscription level and the Contributor role on a single resource group. What effective access does the user have in that resource group?

options.text: Contributor, because a more specific (lower) scope assignment takes precedence for that scope
Reader only, because subscription-level assignments always override resource group assignments
No access, because the two assignments conflict
Owner, because the roles are combined and elevated

questions.explanation: RBAC role assignments are additive, and a role granted at a narrower scope such as a resource group applies fully within that scope alongside the broader Reader role elsewhere.

questions.question: Management wants to guarantee that no one, including subscription owners, can accidentally delete a production virtual network. What should be configured on the resource?

options.text: Removal of the Owner role assignment

questions.explanation: A CanNotDelete lock prevents the resource from being deleted regardless of a user's RBAC permissions, though modifications are still allowed.

questions.question: An organization must ensure that every new storage account deployed anywhere in a subscription automatically has a specific SKU enforced, and any non-compliant deployment is blocked. Which governance tool should be used?

options.text: Azure Policy with a deny effect

questions.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates resource properties against defined rules and can deny deployments that do not comply, such as an unapproved storage SKU.

questions.question: An administrator needs to organize resources for billing separation between two departments while also applying a consistent Azure Policy across both departments' subscriptions. Which two actions accomplish this? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a separate subscription for each department
Place both subscriptions under a shared management group and assign the policy there
Apply a resource lock to each subscription
Create a single resource group shared by both departments

questions.explanation: Separate subscriptions give each department its own billing boundary, and a management group above both subscriptions lets a policy be assigned once and inherited by all subscriptions under it.

questions.question: Finance wants an automatic notification when a resource group's monthly spend is projected to exceed a set amount, before the month ends. What should be configured?

options.text: A budget with an alert threshold in Cost Management
A resource lock on the resource group

questions.explanation: A Cost Management budget with an alert can notify stakeholders when actual or forecasted spend crosses a defined threshold.

questions.question: A user reports they cannot tell why they have access to modify a virtual machine when they were only ever added to a security group. What should the administrator check to understand the source of that access?

options.text: The role assignments and their inherited scope, including group-based assignments, in Access control (IAM)

questions.explanation: Access control (IAM) shows all role assignments including those inherited through group membership and scope, which explains where the effective permission came from.

questions.question: A web application needs to give a third-party service temporary, time-limited access to upload files to a single blob container without sharing the storage account key. What should be used?

options.text: A shared access signature (SAS) scoped to the container with an expiry time
An NSG rule on the storage account

questions.explanation: A SAS token grants delegated, time-limited access with specific permissions to a resource such as a container, without exposing the account key.

questions.question: An administrator wants the ability to revoke all previously issued SAS tokens for a container at once if a token is suspected of being compromised, without regenerating the storage account keys. What should be configured?

options.text: A stored access policy on the container

questions.explanation: A stored access policy centralizes SAS permissions and expiry on the server side, so revoking or modifying the policy immediately invalidates SAS tokens tied to it.

questions.question: A company needs an on-premises file server share to be accessible from Azure VMs while preserving individual Active Directory user permissions on files, rather than relying on the storage account key for everyone. Which Azure Files feature should be used?

options.text: Identity-based authentication for Azure Files with Active Directory
A shared access signature for the file share
Storage account access keys distributed to each user

questions.explanation: Identity-based authentication lets Azure Files enforce NTFS-style permissions tied to Active Directory identities instead of a shared account key.

questions.question: A business requires that data in a storage account remains available even if an entire Azure region becomes unavailable, and reads should still be possible from the secondary region during an outage. Which redundancy option should be selected?
questions.explanation: RA-GRS replicates data to a paired secondary region and allows read access to that secondary copy, providing protection against a full regional outage.

questions.question: An administrator wants blobs older than 90 days that are infrequently accessed to automatically move to a cheaper storage tier, and blobs older than 365 days to be deleted, without manual intervention. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: Lifecycle management policies define rule-based actions, such as tiering or deletion, that run automatically based on a blob's age or last access time.

questions.question: An administrator needs to migrate a large volume of files from an on-premises server into Azure Blob Storage as efficiently as possible from the command line. Which tool is best suited for this task?
questions.explanation: AzCopy is a command-line utility purpose-built for high-performance copying of data into and out of Azure Storage.

questions.question: A team accidentally overwrote a blob with an incorrect version and needs to restore the previous version of that specific blob without restoring the entire container from backup. Which feature should have been enabled in advance to make this possible?
questions.explanation: Blob versioning automatically keeps prior versions of a blob whenever it is modified, allowing an earlier version to be restored.

questions.question: An administrator wants a storage account to reject all traffic from the public internet except for connections originating from the organization's two office IP address ranges. What should be configured?

options.text: Azure Storage firewall rules that allow only the specified IP ranges
A shared access signature limited to those IP ranges

questions.explanation: Storage account firewall settings can restrict network access to selected virtual networks and specific public IP address ranges, denying all other traffic by default.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: An administrator has a working ARM template for a virtual network and wants to adopt a more concise, readable authoring language while deploying the same resources. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Convert the ARM template to a Bicep file and deploy that instead
Rewrite the deployment entirely as a PowerShell script with no template
Deploy the ARM template twice to two regions
Add more parameters to the ARM template

questions.explanation: Bicep is a domain-specific language that compiles to ARM JSON, and Azure tooling supports converting an existing ARM template to Bicep for more concise authoring.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A compliance requirement states that disk encryption keys for a virtual machine must never be stored on the same host as the encrypted data, including temporary and cache disks. Which feature should be enabled?
questions.explanation: Encryption at host encrypts data on the physical host itself, including temp and cache disks, ensuring data is encrypted end-to-end outside the VM's OS.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A virtual machine was originally deployed into the wrong resource group. The administrator needs to relocate it without recreating it from scratch. What should be done?

options.text: Use the move operation to move the VM to the correct resource group
Delete the VM and redeploy it
Apply a resource lock to the VM

questions.explanation: Azure supports moving supported resources, including VMs, between resource groups, subscriptions, or regions using the move operation without recreating the resource.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A database workload on a VM is consistently running low on CPU and memory during peak hours. The disk configuration is adequate. What is the most direct fix?

options.text: Resize the VM to a larger size
Move the VM to another availability zone

questions.explanation: CPU and memory constraints are addressed by changing the VM size to one with more of those resources; disk changes would not resolve a compute bottleneck.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: An application must remain available even if an entire datacenter within a region experiences a power failure. Multiple VM instances need to be spread across physically separate datacenters within one region. What should be used?
questions.explanation: Availability zones are physically separate datacenters within a region, each with independent power and networking, providing protection against a single datacenter failure.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A web tier needs to automatically add or remove VM instances based on CPU load throughout the day. Which service should be deployed?
questions.explanation: Virtual Machine Scale Sets manage a group of identical VMs and support autoscaling rules that add or remove instances based on metrics such as CPU load.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A team wants to store and version their custom container images so they can be pulled during deployments to Azure Container Apps. What should they provision first?
questions.explanation: Azure Container Registry stores and manages private container images, which can then be referenced by services such as Container Apps or Container Instances.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A company wants to host a custom domain, such as www.contoso.com, for a web app running in Azure App Service and needs traffic to be encrypted in transit. Besides mapping the custom domain, what else must be configured?

options.text: A TLS/SSL certificate bound to the custom domain

questions.explanation: Encrypting traffic to a custom domain requires configuring a TLS/SSL certificate and binding it to that hostname on the App Service.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: A development team wants to test a new version of a web app in production-like conditions and be able to swap it into production with minimal downtime if it performs well. What App Service feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Deployment slots allow a separate, live App Service environment for staging a new version, which can then be swapped into production with minimal downtime.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
questions.question: An App Service web app must not be reachable from the public internet and should only be accessible from resources inside a specific virtual network. Which configuration area should the administrator focus on?

options.text: The App Service networking settings, such as private endpoints or VNet integration

questions.explanation: App Service networking features, including private endpoints and virtual network integration, control whether the app is reachable from the public internet or only from within a VNet.

questions.question: Two virtual networks in different regions, each belonging to the same organization, need to communicate privately with low latency without routing traffic over the public internet or through a VPN gateway. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: VNet peering connects two virtual networks directly over the Microsoft backbone network, enabling private, low-latency communication without a gateway.

questions.question: Traffic destined for an on-premises network from a subnet must be forced through a network virtual appliance instead of taking the default route. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: User-defined routes override Azure's default system routes, allowing traffic to be directed through a specific next hop such as a network virtual appliance.

questions.question: An administrator needs to allow inbound RDP access to a specific VM only from the corporate office IP range and deny it from everywhere else. What should be configured on the VM's subnet or network interface?

options.text: A network security group (NSG) rule scoped to the corporate IP range

questions.explanation: NSGs filter inbound and outbound traffic to resources using rules based on source, destination, port, and protocol, which can restrict RDP to a specific IP range.

questions.question: A VM is unreachable on port 443, and multiple NSGs are applied at both the subnet and network interface level. What tool should the administrator use to determine which specific rule is blocking the traffic?

options.text: Effective security rules in Network Watcher

questions.explanation: The effective security rules view combines all NSGs applied at the subnet and NIC level to show the actual rule set affecting traffic, making it possible to identify what's blocking a connection.

questions.question: Administrators need to securely RDP or SSH into VMs that have no public IP addresses, without deploying a jump box or opening inbound NSG rules from the internet. What should be deployed?
questions.explanation: Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP and SSH connectivity to VMs over TLS through the Azure portal, without requiring a public IP on the VM or inbound internet rules.

questions.question: A storage account should only be reachable from resources inside a specific subnet, using its private IP address, rather than the storage account's public endpoint. What should be configured?

options.text: A private endpoint for the storage account

questions.explanation: A private endpoint assigns the PaaS resource a private IP address within the VNet, allowing traffic to stay on the private network instead of the public endpoint.

questions.question: A company wants to host its own DNS zone for contoso.com within Azure and manage records for internal and external resources centrally. Which service should be used?
questions.explanation: Azure DNS is a hosting service for DNS domains that provides name resolution using Microsoft's Azure infrastructure.

questions.question: Backend VMs behind a load balancer are showing as unhealthy, and no traffic is being distributed to them even though the VMs themselves are running normally. What is the most likely area to check first?

options.text: The load balancer's health probe configuration
Resource locks on the resource group

questions.explanation: A misconfigured health probe (wrong port, path, or protocol) will cause a load balancer to mark otherwise healthy backend instances as unavailable and stop sending them traffic.

questions.question: An administrator wants to be automatically notified, and have a webhook triggered, whenever a VM's CPU utilization exceeds 90% for 5 minutes. What should be configured in Azure Monitor?

options.text: An alert rule with an associated action group

questions.explanation: An Azure Monitor alert rule evaluates a metric condition, such as CPU threshold, and an associated action group defines the response, such as a notification or webhook call.

questions.question: An administrator needs to write a query against collected log data to find all failed sign-in events over the past 24 hours across several resources. Which Azure Monitor feature should be used?

options.text: Log Analytics with a Kusto Query Language (KQL) query

questions.explanation: Log Analytics stores collected log data and is queried using Kusto Query Language to search, filter, and analyze events such as failed sign-ins.

questions.question: A company needs to back up several Azure VMs on a recurring schedule and be able to restore them to a point in time if data becomes corrupted. What must be created first to store these backups?

options.text: A storage account with blob versioning

questions.explanation: A Recovery Services vault is the container used by Azure Backup to store recovery points and manage backup policies for VMs and other supported workloads.

questions.question: A company wants a secondary copy of its production VMs continuously replicated to another region so that, in the event of a regional outage, they can fail over and bring the workload online in that region. Which service accomplishes this?
questions.explanation: Azure Site Recovery continuously replicates VMs to a secondary region and orchestrates failover so workloads can be brought online there during an outage.
